critical_signals.title: Luke Miels takes over as CEO, Walmsley exits by Sept 2026
critical_signals.what_happened: Luke Miels became CEO on 1 January 2026, succeeding Emma Walmsley, who left the Board on 31 December 2025 with her employment ending 30 September 2026.
critical_signals.evidence: Luke Miels assumes CEO role 1 January 2026; Emma Walmsley steps down from Board 31 December 2025, employment ends 30 September 2026
critical_signals.ai_hypothesis: A new CEO in his first full year typically re-examines commercial models, vendor rosters and cost structures, which likely aligns with the concurrently announced savings program and Accelerate Growth pipeline focus.
critical_signals.so_what: Leadership transitions open windows for new agency and services relationships as priorities and budgets are reset around the incoming CEO's agenda.
critical_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: A CEO transition is the moment to position Company's DAAI and Omnichannel offerings as enablers of the Accelerate Growth strategy; early engagement can secure preferred-vendor status before rosters are finalized.
critical_signals.next_best_action: Map Miels's public priorities from the FY2025 and Q2 2026 statements and craft an executive briefing linking Company services to his stated Specialty and pipeline focus.
critical_signals.if_no_action: Vendor rosters reset around the incoming CEO's agenda, and Company would not be at that table. Competitors that brief Miels's team first frame the savings and Accelerate Growth agenda, leaving Company to defend legacy scope.
critical_signals.why_now: Miels has held the CEO role since 1 January 2026, and Walmsley's exit completes on 30 September 2026. The handover is in flight, and the rosters that define the new model get set during it.
critical_signals.nba_outcome: Company delivers an executive briefing connecting its services to Miels's stated Specialty and pipeline priorities.
critical_signals.expected_outcome: Company secures preferred-vendor status before rosters finalize around the new CEO. The Accelerate Growth agenda appears in every GSK account conversation this planning year.

critical_signals.title: GSK completes $10.6bn Nuvalent acquisition, expanding NSCLC pipeline
critical_signals.what_happened: GSK completed its acquisition of Nuvalent for approximately $10.6 billion, adding lung cancer assets zidesamtinib, neladalkib and NVL-330.
critical_signals.evidence: Aggregate equity value approximately $10.6 billion (£8.0 billion); adds zidesamtinib, neladalkib and NVL-330 for NSCLC
critical_signals.ai_hypothesis: Integrating three NSCLC assets will require rapid buildout of oncology medical, regulatory and commercial infrastructure, plausibly straining internal capacity and creating outsourcing demand.
critical_signals.so_what: A multi-asset oncology acquisition signals near-term launch preparation needs across medical communications, regulatory submissions and HCP engagement.
critical_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: Post-acquisition integration is a prime opening for Company MedComm, MLR and Regulatory ops to support the incoming NSCLC portfolio, and DAAI to integrate Nuvalent data assets.
critical_signals.next_best_action: Prepare an oncology-launch enablement proposal targeting the newly acquired NSCLC assets and route it to GSK oncology commercial and medical leads.
critical_signals.if_no_action: Nuvalent's three NSCLC assets get staffed with incumbents while integration teams are forming. GSK staffs the oncology buildout with partners already inside, and the new portfolio's commercial frame forms without Company.
critical_signals.why_now: The acquisition has just closed, and integration is being staffed at its most flexible point.
critical_signals.nba_outcome: Company lands an oncology-launch enablement proposal on the new NSCLC portfolio with GSK oncology leadership.
critical_signals.expected_outcome: Company wins a named role on the integration work plan for zidesamtinib, neladalkib or NVL-330 before the assets reach launch planning.

positive_signals.title: Shingrix sets record quarter above £1bn

positive_signals.evidence: Shingrix delivered more than £1.0bn, up 20%, a record for quarterly sales; HIV sales £1.8bn (+10%)
positive_signals.ai_hypothesis: Record shingles-vaccine demand and continued international expansion imply sustained investment in HCP and consumer engagement to defend and grow share.

positive_signals.title: Bepirovirsen posts unprecedented hepatitis B functional cure rates
positive_signals.what_happened: Phase III B-Well trials showed bepirovirsen achieved a 19% functional cure in the overall population and 26% in lower-viral-activity patients versus 0% for standard of care.
positive_signals.evidence: 19% functional cure in the overall study population and 26% in patients with lower viral activity compared to 0% with standard of care only
positive_signals.ai_hypothesis: A potential first-in-class functional cure for chronic hepatitis B likely drives a major global launch requiring heavy medical education and payer engagement.
positive_signals.so_what: Positive pivotal data de-risks a high-value launch and signals imminent commercialization scale-up needs.
positive_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: Company MedComm and Omnichannel can support HCP and patient education for a novel functional-cure narrative, with MLR handling high-volume promotional review.
positive_signals.next_best_action: Develop a hepatitis B launch-readiness concept aligned to the October 2026 PDUFA date and share with GSK Specialty/hepatology teams.
positive_signals.if_no_action: Hepatitis B launch content is built around a novel functional-cure narrative without Company's medical education depth. GSK's specialty team contracts the pre-PDUFA workload to whoever arrives before October 2026.
positive_signals.why_now: Phase III data just landed, and the October 2026 PDUFA fixes the commercialization timeline. The pre-approval content window is open now.
positive_signals.nba_outcome: Company shares a hepatitis B launch-readiness concept aligned to the October 2026 PDUFA with GSK hepatology teams.
positive_signals.expected_outcome: Company holds the HCP and patient education brief for the functional-cure narrative before approval. MLR capacity stands ready for the first wave of promotional claims.

positive_signals.title: Specialty Medicines drives double-digit growth led by Nucala COPD and HIV
positive_signals.what_happened: Q2 2026 Specialty Medicines rose 14%, led by the continued launch of Nucala in COPD and HIV medicines Cabenuva and Dovato.
positive_signals.evidence: Specialty Medicines +14% led by continued launch of Nucala in COPD and HIV medicines Cabenuva and Dovato
positive_signals.ai_hypothesis: Active launches in COPD and HIV imply ongoing demand for launch-phase content, field enablement and omnichannel orchestration.
positive_signals.so_what: The Specialty engine is GSK's growth core and the highest-priority target for commercialization services.
positive_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: Company Omnichannel and MedComm can accelerate the Nucala COPD and HIV launches; DAAI can sharpen HCP targeting across the Specialty portfolio.
positive_signals.next_best_action: Build a Specialty-portfolio omnichannel proposal centered on the Nucala COPD launch curve.
positive_signals.if_no_action: The Nucala COPD launch curve is built by whichever vendor anchors the Specialty account first. HIV momentum behind Cabenuva and Dovato gets sourced separately, and Company's Specialty share fragments.
positive_signals.why_now: Q2 growth of 14% just confirmed Specialty as the growth core, and launch-phase budgets follow that print.
positive_signals.nba_outcome: Company builds a Specialty-portfolio omnichannel proposal centered on the Nucala COPD launch curve.
positive_signals.expected_outcome: Company lands a named role on the Nucala COPD launch and at least one HIV brand. HCP targeting across the Specialty portfolio measurably sharpens within two quarters.

negative_signals.evidence: General Medicines down 6% in Q1, driven by declining sales of the older established portfolio

negative_signals.if_no_action: Declining General Medicines spend is cut further, and Company's mature-brand scope runs off with it. The shift to Specialty and Vaccines happens without a Company role in the redeployment.

negative_signals.nba_outcome: Company proposes a low-cost delivery model for mature-brand maintenance.
negative_signals.expected_outcome: Company stays retained on General Medicines scope at a lower cost point or redeploys explicitly into Specialty work. Budget is freed for growth franchises without revenue loss to Company.

negative_signals.title: Zantac litigation resolved for up to $2.2bn
negative_signals.what_happened: GSK agreed to pay up to $2.2 billion to resolve roughly 80,000 US state court product liability cases over Zantac, with no admission of liability.
negative_signals.evidence: GSK will make an aggregate payment of up to $2.2 billion to resolve all U.S. state court product liability cases, with no admission of liability
negative_signals.ai_hypothesis: Resolving major litigation removes an overhang and likely frees management focus and capital toward pipeline and commercial investment.
negative_signals.so_what: Litigation closure reduces distraction and strengthens the case for offensive commercial spending.
negative_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: Reduced legal overhang supports GSK's pivot to growth investment, indirectly favoring Company's launch and commercialization services; heightened liability awareness also elevates the value of rigorous MLR review.
negative_signals.next_best_action: Reference GSK's compliance sensitivity when positioning Company MLR and promotional-review rigor.
negative_signals.if_no_action: The compliance proof point is never raised while GSK's heightened liability awareness reshapes vendor expectations. Competitors that lead with review rigor capture the promotional compliance briefs.
negative_signals.why_now: The $2.2bn settlement is fresh, and GSK's liability awareness sits at its highest point right now.
negative_signals.nba_outcome: Company positions MLR and promotional-review rigor as a compliance asset in GSK conversations.
negative_signals.expected_outcome: GSK vendor evaluations cite Company as a compliance-grade review partner. Promotional review scope is won or retained because of documented rigor.

risk_signals.title: Roy Jakobs joins GSK Board as Non-Executive Director
risk_signals.what_happened: Roy Jakobs, CEO of Royal Philips, joined the GSK Board as a Non-Executive Director from 13 July 2026.
risk_signals.evidence: GSK's board-information page lists Jakobs as a Non-Executive Director, effective 13 July 2026.
risk_signals.ai_hypothesis: Adding a health-technology CEO to the board may reinforce GSK's digital and AI agenda and influence technology-partner expectations.
risk_signals.so_what: Board-level tech expertise can elevate scrutiny and ambition around digital and data initiatives.
risk_signals.why_it_matters_to_indegene: A tech-oriented board voice strengthens the case for Company's DAAI and Tech Solutions offerings and raises the bar for digital sophistication.
risk_signals.next_best_action: Sharpen Company's DAAI and Tech Solutions positioning to match a more tech-forward GSK board agenda.
risk_signals.if_no_action: The digital bar at GSK rises while Company's DAAI positioning stays generic. A tech-forward board agenda gets met by competitors who speak AI natively.
risk_signals.why_now: Jakobs joined the Board on 13 July 2026, and his arrival is shaping the digital agenda this quarter.
risk_signals.nba_outcome: Company sharpens DAAI and Tech Solutions positioning to match the more tech-forward board.
risk_signals.expected_outcome: Company's AI and data offerings benchmark as board-caliber in GSK conversations. Vendor evaluations recognize Company's digital sophistication by the next procurement cycle.
